Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

Key findings: Middle-aged man with T2DM, HTN and overweight status presenting with acute viral-type symptoms (cough, rhinorrhoea, sore throat, myalgias, subjective fever) and modest dyspnoea. No red-flag features (no chest pain, haemoptysis, persistent diarrhoea, or severe systemic compromise). No objective vitals obtained due to telephone consult.

Differential diagnoses (consistent with transcript and DDx):  
• Acute viral upper respiratory infection / influenza-like illness (including COVID-19) – High likelihood: typical constellation of symptoms over 5 days.  
• Community-acquired pneumonia – Moderate likelihood: increasing dyspnoea and purulent sputum, diabetic risk factor; no objective exam to confirm.  
• Acute bronchitis – Moderate likelihood: sub-acute cough following presumed URI.

Working diagnosis: Probable acute viral URTI; possible early bacterial lower respiratory tract infection.

Management Plan

- Provided advice for conservative management: rest, maintain hydration, regular Paracetamol for fever/discomfort.  
- Issued delayed prescription for antibiotics (Amoxicillin – “one tablet three times daily,” dose not documented) to start if no improvement in 24–48 hours or worsening breathlessness.  
- Safety-net: review or return next week if no improvement or earlier if deterioration.  
- Reinforced smoking cessation efforts (vaping as step-down) and moderation of alcohol intake.  
- No immediate investigations ordered; clinician to reassess need for CXR or labs if symptoms persist.  

Consider:

- Allied health referral (EPC – 10 visits): Not recorded.  
- Reproductive or sexual health clinic referral: Not recorded.  
- Mental health support if indicated (e.g., psychologist, AMS support): Not recorded.  
- CTG registration: Not recorded.  
- Preventive health follow-up booked (e.g., flu vaccine, Pap test): Not recorded.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):

1. Acute viral upper respiratory infection / Influenza-like illness (High) – Sudden onset cough, rhinorrhoea, myalgias, feverishness over 5 days.  
2. Community-acquired pneumonia (Moderate) – Dyspnoea, “mucky” sputum, subjective fevers; risk factors include T2DM and smoking.  
3. Acute bronchitis (Moderate) – Sub-acute cough following URI, minimal systemic toxicity; overlaps with viral URTI.

Quality checks (always include at bottom of note):

● Missing clinically expected elements: objective vital signs (BP, pulse, temp, SpO₂), BMI/waist, immunisation review (influenza/COVID boosters), urinalysis for protein (given T2DM), alcohol/smoking quantity in standard units, mental health screening, medication doses.  
● No internal contradictions identified between transcript and DDx.  
● Transcript quality: Clear but telephone format limited objective examination data; conversational diversions required filtering.
